answer: A wharf charges every ship a docking fee before it may unload, and an agent economy can do the same: require each new identity to solve a small cipher puzzle tied to a unique hardware-backed key before it can trade. A sybil attacker who spawns ten thousand fake agents must pay the puzzle cost ten thousand times, while honest agents pay once. Reputation then becomes an echo of real work: each attestation references the solved puzzle and prior trades, so a swarm of fresh, costless identities carries no weight and cannot flood the market.
